what_happened: The job "Dispatch jobs from a stable ref so merges don't disturb running jobs" (20261018-095726-r3bn) failed during planning, before any code was written. After round 3 of 3 the critic still said the plan needed revising. It judged the approach sound: remove the resync_onto_merge call at gh.rs:1630, cut the pull request head onto the remote tip with Git::replay, and add a `source` field on PrLink. It found one major gap. The plan's criterion 1 demonstration needs a fake Remote or host passed into Athena::land_pr. That function builds GitRemote on "origin" and GhClient itself, requires a github.com remote URL, and has no test harness, so the producer would have to invent a seam the plan never describes. It also listed four smaller points. (1) gh.rs is not among the reading's deliverables (minor). (2) The criterion 2 claim about B's head conflicts with how replay records commits (minor). (3) The signs_commits open question could already be closed (minor). (4) The claim that clippy catches leftover dead code does not hold for pub items (nit). The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered.
cause: The planning stage writes demonstrations for each criterion without checking that the code under test can be driven that way. Nothing in the plan template makes it name the seam, fixture or harness each demonstration uses, or confirm that it exists or say which change adds it. The critic can see this only by reading the code, so it surfaced late. The scope gap (gh.rs not in the reading's deliverables) comes from the same cause: the reading was fixed before anyone traced where the fault lives. The three-round cap has no fallback. It does not require major findings to shrink, and it keeps no partial plan, so a gap that appears late fails the job. The earlier case 20261018-100226-1mfq failed in planning the same way.
prevention: Change the plan template and planning flow in three ways. (1) Each demonstration must name its test seam: the exact function or constructor it calls, how the fake or fixture is injected, and whether that seam exists today or is a planned change in the plan's own deliverables. (2) The planner must trace the fault to the files that must change, and flag any that are outside the reading's deliverables, before round 1. (3) When the cap is reached with only seam, scope or wording findings left, the system should keep the best plan and send it to the producer with the findings attached as required fixes, or to the operator for one guided revision. It should not fail the job with nothing kept.
proposed_request: Change the planning stage so a plan cannot pass the critic unless every demonstration names its test seam. For each criterion's demonstration, the plan must state the function or constructor the test calls, how any fake remote, host or fixture is injected, and whether that seam already exists or is added by a named deliverable. Have the planner list the files the fix must touch and compare them with the reading's deliverables, flagging any extra file as a scope question in round 1. When the last planning round ends with only minor or nit findings, or with a major finding that is a seam or scope gap, hand the plan to the producer with those findings as mandatory fixes. Do not fail the job. Show this with tests: a plan whose demonstration calls a function that builds its own client is rejected; the same plan with an injection seam in its deliverables passes; a plan that ends round 3 with a seam finding is handed on with the finding attached. Then re-submit the job "Dispatch jobs from a stable ref so merges don't disturb running jobs", with crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs added to the deliverables and a fake Remote and host seam for Athena::land_pr named in the plan.
